target: काम से लौटते हुए रास्ते में सब्ज़ी भी ले ली।
english: On the way back from work, I picked up vegetables too.
reason: Opens with the proverb "एक पंथ दो काज" (proverb/motto register), and "बाज़ार भी कर लिया" is not idiomatic Hindi. Replacement keeps the रास्ते में + compound-verb perfective (ले ली) in an errand a learner actually runs.

english: We flew kites on the roof.
reason: "अटारी" is archaic/rural for a rooftop and the sentence has no subject at all, so the ने-perfective it is teaching is invisible. Replacement keeps the same past-transitive sentence with the everyday word छत and an explicit हमने.

target: जूते बाहर उतारकर वह घर में आ गया।
english: He took his shoes off outside and came into the house.
reason: Translationese for "stepped over the threshold" — "दरवाज़े पर पाँव रखकर" is not how anyone describes entering a house. Replacement keeps the -कर conjunctive participle plus घर में आ गया with a real, very Indian everyday action.

target: हमारे परिवार में सब मिलकर खाना खाते हैं।
english: In our family we all eat together.
reason: Moralising social-message line about gender discrimination — reads like a school textbook slogan, not speech. Replacement keeps the हमारे परिवार में + habitual present frame with an ordinary family fact.

target: हमारे यहाँ होली बहुत धूमधाम से मनाई जाती है।
english: Where we live, Holi is celebrated with a lot of fanfare.
reason: Textbook almanac trivia; "फागुन" is a Hindu-calendar month name a beginner will never need or use. Replacement keeps the same passive मनाई जाती है with vocabulary a learner can actually deploy.

target: बातें करते हुए हम घर पहुँच गए।
english: Chatting along the way, we got home.
reason: "नाव खेना" (to row a boat) is niche literary vocabulary no learner will ever use. Replacement keeps the -ते हुए simultaneous participle with an everyday action.

target: उसे घर में चप्पल पहनने की आदत है।
english: She's in the habit of wearing slippers indoors.
reason: Encyclopaedia-style line about the antiquity of a tradition — pointless trivia in a stilted written register. Replacement keeps the -ने की + noun construction in ordinary spoken Hindi.

target: आशीष हमारी क्लास में सबसे लंबा लड़का है।
english: Ashish is the tallest boy in our class.
reason: Fabricated trivia — nobody claims someone is the tallest man in Chandigarh. Replacement keeps the सबसे + adjective superlative in a setting a learner would really talk about.

target: प्रिया अपनी क्लास में सबसे लंबी लड़की है।
english: Priya is the tallest girl in her class.
reason: Same fabricated "tallest woman in Bhopal" trivia, and "औरत" is blunter than the polite register being taught. Replacement keeps the feminine सबसे superlative agreement in a natural context.

target: यह बैग उस बैग से भारी है।
english: This bag is heavier than that one.
reason: Pointless produce trivia — comparing the weight of jackfruit and mango is not something anyone says. Replacement keeps the X से भारी comparative in a situation that comes up constantly (packing, shopping, travel).

target: यह होटल उस होटल जितना महँगा नहीं है।
english: This hotel isn't as expensive as that one.
reason: Awkward impersonal passive ("पसंद नहीं किया जाता") about vegetable popularity — translationese trivia. Replacement keeps the जितना ... नहीं equative comparison in natural spoken form.

target: प्रिंसिपल ने आज बच्चों को छुट्टी दे दी।
english: The principal gave the kids a holiday today.
reason: Bureaucratic press-release register ("प्राचार्य", "वार्षिक उत्सव का उद्घाटन") — none of it is everyday speech. Replacement keeps the ने-perfective with a school-related event in ordinary spoken vocabulary.
